title: nginx 1.31's json_set directive rejects a bad webhook payload about 13 times faster than forwarding it
why_read: A concrete, well-measured performance benchmark of nginx's new native JSON parsing module versus backend-side validation, useful for real production decisions.
analysis: This post benchmarks nginx 1.31's new ngx_http_json_module, which lets nginx read and validate fields from a JSON request body directly, before forwarding it to a backend application. The author measured about a 13x speedup in rejecting malformed webhook payloads compared to letting a Python backend do the same validation. It also covers new related features like predicate-based location matching and early body reads, which together allow routing decisions based on payload content rather than just the URL. This is a useful, data-backed piece for anyone running high-volume webhook or API gateways who wants to reduce backend load from invalid requests.
